selection: All newly discovered matching records in this collection; no fixed paper-count quota.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and two-sample Mendelian randomization reveal CD4 + T cell-expressed COMT and JUN as shared candidate genes for Alzheimer's disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
papers.authors: Ou C, Chen B, Yu H, Deng J, Long H.
papers.abstract: BackgroundAlzheimer's disease (AD) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are high-burden diseases; T2DM independently elevates AD risk via shared pathogenesis, yet their shared peripheral immune pathways and genetically supported cell-specific targets remain undefined.ObjectiveTo identify shared immune subsets, key genes and candidate compounds for AD and T2DM via integrated scRNA-seq and two-sample Mendelian randomization.MethodsWe constructed an integrated multi-omics framework combining peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and two-sample Mendelian randomization (2SMR) using 10 public GEO datasets, with core analyses covering cell annotation, cell-cell communication profiling, differential expression analysis, eQTL-based 2SMR, in silico gene function prediction, and molecular docking with dynamics simulation for compound screening.ResultsCD4 + T cells were inferred as the most abundant adaptive immune subset and a potential intercellular communication hub in peripheral blood of both AD and T2DM. Dual scRNA-seq/2SMR screening identified consistently upregulated shared candidate genes COMT and JUN , validated at single-cell and bulk transcriptome levels; myricetin and tauroursodeoxycholic acid were screened as candidate compounds with high predicted binding affinity to the encoded proteins. The 100 ns molecular dynamics simulation confirmed favorable structural stability of the COMT -myricetin complex (RMSD ∼1.2 Å).ConclusionsAs an exploratory bioinformatics investigation, this study proposes a testable hypothesis that CD4 + T cells and the COMT / JUN axis may act as a potential shared immune regulatory node in the concurrent pathogenesis of AD and T2DM, differing from the canonical T cell-driven pathological process in classic autoimmune diseases. All findings remain preliminary and require dedicated experimental validation.

papers.title: RHOA-ROCK hyperactivation is associated with impaired migratory persistence and an effector-associated phenotype in aged CD8 + T cells.
papers.authors: Kan S, Jiang W, Hu Z, Wang S, Lou Y, Jin J.
papers.abstract: Background Immune aging is characterized by impaired immune memory, manifested as increased susceptibility to previously encountered pathogens and reduced vaccine efficacy, yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated whether age-related RHOA hyperactivation, together with reduced migratory persistence, skews the fate decision of CD8 + T cells away from memory commitment toward terminal effector differentiation. Methods Naïve CD8 + T cells were isolated from peripheral blood of young and older healthy donors. Clustering capacity and migratory persistence were assessed by Incucyte live-cell imaging and single-cell trajectory tracking. Differentiation phenotypes were analyzed by flow cytometry. Single-cell RNA sequencing and module scoring were performed to identify key molecular pathways, with validation by Western blotting. Pharmacological inhibition of RHOA-ROCK pathway and mechanical cluster disruption were used to establish causal relationships. Results In qualitative assays, Aged CD8 + T cells formed fewer activation-induced clusters in vitro and displayed reduced migratory persistence relative to young cells. Flow cytometry revealed accelerated effector differentiation in aged CD8 + T cells, accompanied by diminished memory commitment. Single-cell RNA sequencing uncovered a transcriptional signature consistent with RHOA hyperactivation, together with elevated senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) and exhaustion signatures and dysregulated cytoskeletal dynamics. Biochemical assays confirmed elevated RHOA activity (GTP-bound RHOA) and sustained cofilin phosphorylation, the latter indicating cofilin inactivation and impaired actin depolymerization. GSEA showed enrichment of mTORC1 signaling and concomitant suppression of WNT/β-catenin signaling in aged CD8 + T cells, consistent with a cell-fate bias toward terminal effector differentiation at the expense of memory commitment. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of RHOA-ROCK pathway restored CD62L and CD127 expression in aged CD8 + T cells, consistent with at least partial restoration of an effector-associated phenotype. Conclusion In aged CD8 + T cells, RHOA hyperactivation impairs cofilin-mediated actin depolymerization, compromising activation-induced clustering and sustaining mTORC1 signaling while repressing WNT/β-catenin-dependent memory programs, thereby skewing differentiation toward a terminal effector fate. Pharmacological inhibition of RHOA-ROCK pathway partially reverses these alterations, suggesting that this pathway may represent a potential therapeutic target for counteracting CD8 + T cell immune aging.

papers.title: Distinct cellular source and bulk immune correlates of HAVCR2 expression in seminoma.
papers.authors: Kim SH, Lee DY, Kim MG, Jung MJ, Han TW, Yang HJ, Kim DS, Kim HJ, Lee CH, Jeon YS, Lee JH, Kim KH.
papers.abstract: HAVCR2 (T-cell immunoglobulin and mucin domain-containing protein 3; TIM-3) expression is associated with favorable prognosis in seminoma, but its underlying immune context remains unclear. We sought to distinguish the cellular source of HAVCR2 from the immune correlates of its interpatient bulk expression using bulk and single-cell transcriptomic datasets. In The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) seminoma discovery cohort (n = 64), we evaluated associations between HAVCR2 expression and eight predefined immune-compartment signatures, adjusting for overall immune infiltration using PTPRC (CD45) and the ESTIMATE algorithm. After adjustment, associations with T-cell-, cytotoxicity-, and checkpoint-related signatures were attenuated or lost, whereas macrophage-related signatures remained correlated with HAVCR2 expression; on mutual adjustment, the general macrophage rather than the M2-associated signature retained this association. In an independent bulk cohort (GSE3218, n = 13), the M2-associated signature remained associated with HAVCR2 after PTPRC adjustment, whereas the general macrophage association was directionally concordant but attenuated after adjustment. Single-cell RNA sequencing of a four-donor seminoma cohort (GSE228501) showed background-level HAVCR2 expression in tumor cells, while HAVCR2-positive cells were detected in macrophage, exhaustion-like CD8 T-cell, and proliferating T-cell compartments, with donor-level mean expression numerically higher in exhaustion-like CD8 T cells than in macrophages. Although HAVCR2 was expressed across multiple immune compartments at the single-cell level, interpatient bulk HAVCR2 expression was associated with a macrophage-related immune context beyond overall immune infiltration, whereas the specific macrophage phenotype remained unresolved. These findings inform the interpretation of bulk HAVCR2 as a biomarker, including its previously reported prognostic association, without implying a causal role for macrophages in clinical outcome.

papers.title: IL-17Rb mediates the pathogenesis of allergic rhinitis through STAT6-dependent regulation of TH2 cells and type 2 inflammatory cytokines.
papers.authors: Wei MY, Liu Z, Chen Q, Li H, Zhang ZQ, Lei WJ, Wu J, Liu Y, Zhu XH.
papers.abstract: Background Allergic rhinitis (AR) is characterized by a T helper 2 (Th2)-cell-mediated immune imbalance, yet its upstream molecular drivers remain poorly defined. Interleukin-17 receptor B (IL-17Rb) has been implicated in type 2 inflammation, but its precise functional role and mechanism in AR pathogenesis are unclear. Objective This study aimed to identify key immunoregulatory genes in AR via bioinformatics and to comprehensively elucidate the functional role and mechanisms of IL-17Rb using both in vivo animal and in vitro cellular models. Methods Candidate genes were screened using GEO datasets and machine learning. An HDM-induced AR murine model and in vitro cell models were utilized. AAV-mediated IL-17Rb knockdown or overexpression, alongside a specific STAT6 inhibitor (AS1517499), were employed. Evaluations included nasal symptoms, histopathology, STAT6 activation, and parameters of Th2 inflammation alongside the Th1/Th17/Treg balance (IL-4/5/13, IFN-γ, IL-17A, IL-10). Results Bioinformatics identified IL-17Rb as a pivotal upregulated gene in AR, correlating with Th2 infiltration (r = 0.74). In vivo, IL-17Rb knockdown alleviated AR symptoms, eosinophil/mast cell infiltration, and type 2 cytokine release. Importantly, it rectified the AR-associated immune imbalance by restoring IFN-γ (Th1) and IL-10 (Treg) while reducing IL-17A (Th17). Conversely, IL-17Rb overexpression exacerbated Th2 inflammation and STAT6 phosphorylation. Co-administration of AS1517499 successfully abrogated these overexpression-induced effects, confirming a STAT6-dependent mechanism. Furthermore, in vitro blockade of IL-17Rb inhibited IL-25-promoted Th2 differentiation and STAT6 activation. Conclusion IL-17Rb is a critical upstream immunoregulator in AR, driving STAT6-dependent Th2 inflammation and broadly modulating the Th1/Th17/Treg balance. Targeting the IL-17Rb/STAT6 axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Identification of Key Fatty acid Metabolism-Related Genes in Vascular Dementia.
papers.authors: Zhu Y, Li M, Shi J, Chen Y.
papers.abstract: Vascular dementia (VaD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by chronic cerebral hypoperfusion and cognitive decline, yet the role of fatty acid metabolism in its pathogenesis remains incompletely understood. Integrated transcriptomic profiling was combined with network-based analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and machine learning to uncover key fatty acid metabolism-associated molecular features associated with VaD. Single-cell RNA sequencing, intercellular communication inference, and in silico perturbation analyses were applied to define immune-stromal interactions. Potential therapeutic compounds were evaluated using molecular docking and dynamics simulations. We identified three VaD-related fatty acid metabolism genes (VaD-FAMRGs), namely PNPLA3, HSP90AA1, and ALB, which showed consistent diagnostic performance across multiple computational approaches and were associated with lipid metabolism, inflammatory processes, and neurovascular unit dysfunction. Functional enrichment, single-cell RNA sequencing, and in silico gene perturbation analyses provided exploratory insights into the potential associations of these candidate genes with lipid transport, metabolic regulation, synaptic maintenance, and immune-inflammatory processes. Cell-cell communication analysis further revealed activation of the ANGPTL signaling axis, suggesting impaired endothelial-glial interactions driven by lipid metabolic dysregulation. Regulatory network analysis identified key transcriptional and post-transcriptional regulators, including REST, miR-155-5p, and miR-21-5p, which may coordinately modulate VaD-FAMRG expression. Drug repurposing analysis highlighted quercetin as a candidate compound with predicted interactions with all three hub proteins, supported by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. These findings suggest that dysregulated fatty acid metabolism may be associated with the development and progression of VaD through coordinated metabolic, inflammatory, and neurovascular mechanisms. This study provides a systems-level framework for understanding the underlying pathological processes and establishes a theoretical basis for future mechanistic and experimental validation.

papers.title: Dual-database pharmacovigilance analysis based on FAERS and JADER combined with network pharmacology to explore fulvestrant-associated respiratory toxicity.
papers.authors: Pan W, Xu Y, Shao Z, Ren X, Xu W.
papers.abstract: Background Fulvestrant serves as cornerstone endocrine therapy for hormone receptor-positive (HR-positive) advanced breast cancer. Recent reports indicate safety concerns regarding respiratory toxicity. This study systematically characterized fulvestrant-related respiratory adverse events (adverse events, AEs) using two independent spontaneous reporting databases (FAERS and JADER) for cross-verification and investigated underlying mechanisms. Methods Disproportionality analysis utilized two post-marketing surveillance databases, the United States Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) and Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report (JADER), applying reporting odds ratio (ROR) and Bayesian confidence propagation neural network (BCPNN) methods for respiratory adverse event signal detection. Fulvestrant targets were predicted using SwissTargetPrediction, TargetNet, and Therapeutic Target Database (TTD). Lung disease-related genes were identified from GeneCards and Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM). Overlapping targets underwent Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analysis. A protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was constructed with STRING and Cytoscape, core genes identified by maximum clique centrality (MCC) algorithm. CB-Dock2 platform performed molecular docking between fulvestrant and key targets. Results A total of 6988 fulvestrant-related reports were included from FAERS with 896 respiratory toxicity cases, while 1582 fulvestrant-associated adverse event reports were retrieved from JADER, covering 154 respiratory toxicity cases. Twenty-two respiratory adverse event signals were detected in FAERS, among which nine consistent positive signals were replicated in JADER, including pleural effusion (ROR = 5.38), interstitial lung disease (ROR = 3.94), and dyspnea (ROR = 1.50). Median time to onset was 70 days (interquartile range 21-227 days). Network pharmacology analysis identified 78 overlapping targets between fulvestrant and lung diseases. Enrichment analysis indicated involvement of inflammatory response, immune regulation, oxidative stress pathways, tumor necrosis factor (TNF) signaling pathway, and interleukin 17 (IL-17) signaling pathway. Molecular docking suggested favorable predicted binding conformations between fulvestrant and several core proteins, including mitogen-activated protein kinase 14 (MAPK14), hypoxia inducible factor 1 subunit alpha (HIF1A), and mitogen-activated protein kinase 1 (MAPK1), although these findings remain computational and require further validation. Conclusion This hypothesis-generating integrated dual-database pharmacovigilance and network pharmacology analysis revealed significant association between fulvestrant and multiple respiratory toxicities, often occurring early during treatment. Potential mechanisms may involve inflammatory response, immune dysregulation, and oxidative stress-related pathways. The molecular docking findings provide exploratory computational support only and do not constitute direct evidence of in vivo interactions or causal mechanisms. Cross-database validation greatly improved the robustness of our analytical results, yet definite causality still cannot be established due to inherent limitations of spontaneous reporting systems. These findings require external validation and experimental verification and provide theoretical basis for clinical risk management and further mechanistic research.

papers.title: Advanced drug delivery strategies for overcoming tumor-mediated molecular hijacking: Emerging nanotherapeutics, advanced biotherapeutics, and artificial intelligence.
papers.authors: Kumar V, Batra P, Das N, Shende P.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in precision oncology fueled the development of nanotherapeutics,​ molecularly targeted drugs, engineered immunotherapies, RNA therapeutics, and smart biomaterials for more selective cancer treatment. However, long-term therapeutic responses remain restricted by interconnected adaptive mechanisms, including ABC transporter-mediated drug efflux, dysregulated signaling pathways, apoptosis evasion, immune escape, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and tumor microenvironment​ remodeling. In this review article, these processes are collectively framed as tumor-mediated molecular hijacking, describing malignant cell exploitation and microenvironmental pathways that promote multidrug resistance and therapeutic failure. The review critically examines nanotherapeutic and advanced biotherapeutic strategies to counteract these mechanisms, including functionalized nanocarriers, antibody-drug conjugates, CAR-T cells, tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy, immune checkpoint blockade, mesenchymal stem-cell (MSC)-based therapeutics, CRISPR-mediated genome editing, bispecific T-cell engagers, and RNA-based approaches. Particular focus includes drug-delivery elements such as tumour penetration, intracellular trafficking, controlled release, pharmacokinetics, biodistribution, and critical formulation attributes, as well as translational challenges such as manufacturability, scalability, reproducibility, stability, safety, and regulatory feasibility. Emerging biofabrication approaches enable the fabrication of adaptive and personalized delivery systems, while artificial intelligence and machine learning are utilized as tools for structure-guided design, nanocarrier optimization, treatment-response prediction, and patient-specific digital-twin modelling. This paper combines tumor-mediated molecular hijacking with drug delivery technology at the forefront and translational aspects to create a comprehensive platform for clinically relevant precision cancer therapeutics.Clinical trial number: Not applicable.

papers.title: CAN-IMMUNE: A Computational Platform to Facilitate Cancer-Specific Neoantigen Identification.
papers.authors: Krishna SSG, Shahbazy M, Mullan KA, Dorvash M, Goncalves G, Aranha R, Munday PR, Jia Y, Faridi P, Purcell AW, Li C.
papers.abstract: Neoantigens are formed due to the somatic mutations that arise during carcinogenesis; they give rise to unique neo-peptides bearing cancer-specific mutations that are presented on the surface of the tumor in complex with human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules for scrutiny by T cells. Some neoepitopes can be recognized by tumoricidal T cells and serve as targets for cancer vaccines and immunotherapies. Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry identifies human leukocyte antigen-presented peptides through spectral matching against reference proteome databases. However, reference proteome databases usually contain only canonical sequences and lack cancer-specific mutations, limiting neoantigen discovery. To tackle this challenge, we developed a comprehensive platform, CAN-IMMUNE, to browse, search, and generate cancer-specific mutant peptide libraries, thereby enabling the identification of mutant peptides during liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry spectral searches. Major highlights of CAN-IMMUNE include (a) 4,531,600 unique mutant peptides across 55 curated cancer types from 2,052 cancer cell lines and 31 tissues documented to facilitate the generation of bespoke cancer-specific mutant peptide libraries, (b) MutPep, a component of CAN-IMMUNE to allow local generation of mutant peptide libraries using inputs from users, and (c) a computational strategy for prioritizing mutant peptides. We showcased the use of CAN-IMMUNE by searching immunopeptidomics datasets of triple-negative breast cancer and melanoma cell lines. Using CAN-IMMUNE libraries, we computationally identified and prioritized mutant peptides not represented in canonical reference proteome searches, thereby providing potential neoantigen candidates for further immunogenicity assessment. We anticipate that CAN-IMMUNE can accelerate the identification of cancer neoantigens for the development of targeted cancer immunotherapies. CAN-IMMUNE is freely available at https://canelib.erc.monash.edu.

papers.title: Targeting AP1S1 modulates the unfolded protein response and cell cycle and sensitizes triple-negative breast cancer to erlotinib.
papers.authors: Gong R, Peng S, Yang Y, Mei D, Jiang S, Gao H, Cheng Y.
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive malignancy lacking actionable therapeutic targets. Intrinsic resistance to tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy remains a major barrier to improving clinical outcomes. Here, we identify adaptor-related protein complex 1 subunit sigma 1 (AP1S1) as an oncogenic regulator and a potential therapeutic vulnerability in TNBC. Through integrated multi-omics profiling and experimental validation, we found that AP1S1 is significantly overexpressed in breast cancer and correlates with advanced clinicopathological features and poor prognosis. Functionally, knockdown of AP1S1 inhibited cell proliferation, induced apoptosis, and triggered cell cycle arrest in vitro and in patient-derived organoids (PDOs). Single-cell RNA sequencing quantitatively confirmed that AP1S1 expression is specifically enriched in malignant cell populations and closely associates with hyperproliferation and stress-response pathways. Molecularly, AP1S1 is involved in a functional network involving both cell cycle progression and the unfolded protein response (UPR), and its high expression correlates with an "immune-desert" microenvironment characterized by depleted effector T cell infiltration. Furthermore, integrating pharmacogenomic analysis with in vitro and PDOs assays, we found that AP1S1 depletion increases the sensitivity of TNBC cells to erlotinib. Collectively, these findings identify AP1S1 as a multifaceted regulator of TNBC aggressiveness and therapy responsiveness, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic target to enhance TKI sensitivity and its association with immune exclusion.

papers.title: Molecular design and target interactions of NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitors: a comprehensive review of synthetic and natural scaffolds (2023-2025).
papers.authors: Boy-Ruiz D, Durán-Peña MJ, Collado IG, Cordero MD, Botubol-Ares JM.
papers.abstract: The NLRP3 inflammasome is a critical innate immune sensor detecting diverse pathogen- and damage-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs/DAMPs). Its activation triggers the maturation and release of the proinflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-18, as well as pyroptotic cell death. Since dysregulated NLRP3 activity drives various autoinflammatory and metabolic diseases, it represents a major therapeutic target. This review provides an updated framework of NLRP3 activation mechanisms, emphasizing the roles of the NACHT and LRR domains in NEK7 recruitment and the PYD domain in ASC recruitment. We identify specific residues within these domains to guide docking-based studies. Furthermore, this review highlights the principal chemical scaffolds of emerging small-molecule NLRP3 inhibitors, both synthetic and natural products, with a focus on clinical candidates and pharmacological profiles. Special attention is given to plant-derived natural products as a source of NLRP3 drug discovery, which has expanded the inhibitor chemical space. Finally, we address future challenges, such as targeting upstream activation signals (e.g., ROS or oxidized DNA interactions), and designing dual inhibitors for multiple inflammasomes (e.g., AIM2, NLRP1, NLRC4) to mitigate inflammasome crosstalk. By integrating detailed mechanistic insights with therapeutic advances, this review aims to catalyze computational studies and accelerate the design of the next generation of safe and stable NLRP3-targeting therapeutics.

papers.title: Role of the Tregs-Endothelial Cell Interaction Network in Immune Microenvironment Remodeling and Targeted Intervention in Cardiovascular Diseases.
papers.authors: Mo L, Gao J, Chen Z, Zeng X, Zhang J, Zhou J, Feng J, Bai Y.
papers.abstract: The pathogenesis of cardiovascular disease (CVD) involves immune and metabolic remodeling of the vascular microenvironment, in which interactions between regulatory T cells (Tregs) and endothelial cells are important. Tregs can support endothelial homeostasis through immunoregulatory cytokines, whereas endothelial signals may influence Treg activity. This network has context-dependent effects in CVD: Tregs suppress inflammation, preserve endothelial barrier integrity, and promote repair, whereas Treg dysfunction, metabolic dysregulation, or age-related changes can impair endothelial function and accelerate disease progression. This review examines how glycolysis-lactate signaling, hypoxic metabolic adaptation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and redox imbalance shape Treg-endothelial crosstalk and immune microenvironment remodeling in CVD. We also discuss molecularly targeted interventions, cell-based and engineering approaches, and metabolic therapies directed at this network. Finally, we consider how spatial and single-cell multi-omics can identify disease-associated Treg and endothelial states, map their interactions, and link transcriptional programs to metabolic dysfunction. This metabolic perspective may guide mechanistic studies and the development of targeted therapies for CVD.

papers.title: Identification of circadian rhythm-related diagnostic biomarkers and immune subtypes in allergic rhinitis based on WGCNA and machine learning approaches.
papers.authors: Wan Z, Jiang L, Wu C.
papers.abstract: Background Allergic rhinitis (AR) is a common chronic inflammatory disease characterized by dysregulated immune responses and pronounced circadian rhythm disturbances. However, the molecular mechanisms linking circadian rhythm-related genes (CRRGs) to AR pathogenesis and immune heterogeneity remain insufficiently understood. Methods Public microarray datasets (GSE75011 and GSE43523) were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between AR patients and healthy controls were identified using the limma package. Circadian rhythm-related DEGs (DECRRGs) were obtained by intersecting DEGs with curated CRRGs. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) was applied to identify AR-related gene modules. Machine learning algorithms, including support vector machine-recursive feature elimination and Boruta, were used to screen diagnostic biomarkers. Immune infiltration was assessed using CIBERSORT and single-sample Gene Set Enrichment Analysis. Single-gene gene set enrichment analysis, non-negative matrix factorization-based molecular subtyping, and competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) network construction were subsequently performed. Results A total of 36 DECRRGs were identified and significantly enriched in immune- and inflammation-related pathways. WGCNA revealed a turquoise module that was strongly correlated with AR. Machine learning analysis identified two key diagnostic biomarkers, BTG1 and IDI1, which demonstrated robust diagnostic performance in both the training set (AUC = 0.781 and 0.755) and the validation set (AUC = 0.986 and 0.857). Immune infiltration analysis revealed significant alterations in immune cell composition between AR and control samples. Non-negative matrix factorization clustering classified AR patients into two distinct molecular subtypes with markedly different immune landscapes. Finally, a ceRNA regulatory network was constructed to elucidate the post-transcriptional regulatory mechanisms of the diagnostic genes. Conclusions This study systematically identified circadian rhythm-related diagnostic biomarkers for AR and revealed immune-based molecular subtypes, providing novel insights into the circadian-immune regulatory mechanisms underlying AR pathogenesis.

papers.title: Mapping the Evolution of T Cell Immunity in Coronary Heart Disease: A Bibliometric Analysis with a Focus on Inflammatory Paradigms (1991-2026).
papers.authors: Hua S, Cen D, Guo J, Zhang J, Si C, Xu P, Zhang A, Wang L.
papers.abstract: Background Coronary heart disease (CHD) remains the leading cause of global cardiovascular mortality. T cell-mediated adaptive immunity, particularly Th1, regulatory T cell (Treg), and Th17 subsets, plays a pivotal role in atherosclerotic plaque formation and destabilisation, yet a systematic, quantitative mapping of this research landscape is lacking. Methods Publications on T cell immunity in CHD from 1991 to August 2026 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection, restricted to English-language original articles. Bibliometric indicators were analysed with Microsoft Excel, VOSviewer (v1.6.20), CiteSpace (v6.4.R1), and bibliometric.com. Co-authorship, keyword co-occurrence, and burst-keyword analyses were performed. Results A total of 761 articles from 5,796 authors across 58 countries/regions and 299 journals were identified. Annual output increased markedly after 2010. China contributed the largest number of articles (n = 255, 33.5%), while the USA led in total citations (n = 8552), followed by China (n = 6,965) and Germany (n = 4,110). The most prolific and most highly cited author was Hansson Goran K. (14 publications; H-index = 13), while Becker AE achieved the highest average citation impact (248.0 citations per article). Circulation (IF = 35.5) was the leading journal by both article count (n = 33) and citations (n = 2,725). Keyword clustering revealed eight major research themes: clinical translation and computational approaches, T cell activation and immune cell interactions, classic immunopathology and plaque biology, inflammation and infectious triggers, Treg biology and T helper subsets, cytokine regulation and apoptosis, plaque vulnerability and ACS, and antigen presentation and extracellular vesicles. Burst analysis identified "machine learning", "monocytes", and "risk" as the most prominent emerging topics since 2023. Conclusion Research on T cell immunity in CHD has grown markedly, with a clear shift toward the macrophage-T cell immune axis and immune-metabolic interactions, together with Treg-based therapeutic strategies and machine learning-assisted risk stratification. These findings provide a descriptive map that may help inform future translational research.

papers.title: T cell transcriptional landscapes are shaped by T cell receptor sequence similarity.
papers.authors: Wang H, Wang H, Ji Z.
papers.abstract: T cells exhibit high heterogeneity in both their gene expression profiles and antigen specificities, but the precise relationship between these two features remains largely unknown. Utilizing a large-scale single-cell immune profiling dataset that includes both T cell receptor (TCR) sequences and gene expression profiles of individual cells, we systematically investigated how the transcriptional profiles of T cells are linked to their TCR sequence similarity. We observed that T cells sharing the same clonotype often belong to the same cell type, and that gene expression similarity among T cells correlates with TCR sequence similarity. Furthermore, we identified features such as clonality, VJ gene usage, sequence motifs, and amino acid preferences that are distinctly associated with specific T cell subtypes. These findings suggest that T cell transcriptional landscapes are broadly shared and influenced by TCR sequence similarity.

papers.title: RNA-binding proteins PCBP1 and PCBP2 are indispensable for B-cell development.
papers.authors: Lin L, Qi T, Zhu L, Li G, Miao C, Chang X.
papers.abstract: B-cell development in the bone marrow is a tightly regulated process requiring precise control of gene expression at both the transcriptional and post-transcriptional levels. Here, we identify the RNA-binding proteins PCBP1 and PCBP2 as critical regulators of early B lymphopoiesis with partially overlapping, dosage-sensitive functions. While a single deficiency of either Pcbp1 or Pcbp2 results in only a partial blockade at the pro-B to pre-B transition, their combined deletion causes a severe defect beginning at the pro-B stage and impairing subsequent development. Using single-cell RNA sequencing, we localize the major bottleneck to the pro-B VDJ A stage, which we propose represents cells undergoing D-JH rearrangement. Mechanistically, Pcbp1/2 deficiency triggers multifaceted cell-intrinsic defects, including downregulation of the Ebf1-dependent lineage program, mitochondrial dysfunction, and accumulation of proteotoxic stress. These defects converge to block early progenitor survival and expansion, ultimately preventing B cells from progressing beyond the pre-B stage. Consistently, single-axis interventions, such as providing a pre-rearranged BCR or scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS), fail to restore development; ROS scavenging improves survival but not expansion. Our findings establish PCBP1 and PCBP2 as critical post-transcriptional regulators that couple metabolic fitness with lineage integrity during early B-cell development.

papers.title: Single-cell multiomics profiling reveals tumour microenvironment landscape and sex-specific immune-suppressive feature in male breast cancer.
papers.authors: Sun H, Wang R, Wang Y, Jiang M, Liu CC, Yang C, Wang Z, Sun B, Zhang J, Zhan M, Fan Z, Li Y, Yu K.
papers.abstract: Background Male breast cancer (MBC) represents a small proportion of all breast cancer (BC) cases, yet it is characterized by a higher rate of lymph node metastasis and poorer prognosis compared to female breast cancer (FBC). However, limited research has been conducted on MBC primarily due to its rarity and the technological constraints. Methods To address this, we performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) on samples from 16 MBC patients (87 518 cells) and imaging mass cytometry (IMC) on samples from 42 patients (265 137 cells), enabling a comprehensive analysis of the MBC microenvironment at both single-cell transcriptome and protein levels. Results At the autosomal level, the MBC tumor cells and their microenvironment exhibit distinct characteristics. We found that PDZ binding kinase (PBK) expression was elevated in MBC tumor cells and linked to proliferation-related programs, whereas SRY-Box transcription factor 4 (SOX4) expression was increased in endothelial cells and associated with endothelial-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) signatures and metastatic potential. Additionally, IMC analysis revealed notable differences in the spatial features of the tumor microenvironment between MBC and FBC. Regarding sex-chromosomal regulation, the lysine demethylase 5D (KDM5D) gene originating from the Y chromosome was associated with cGAS/STING protein abundance and reduced immune cell infiltration in MBC. Conclusion In conclusion, both autosomal and sex-chromosomal regulation may collectively contribute to the modulation of microenvironmental differences between MBC and FBC. Whether KDM5D is functionally linked to cGAS/STING signaling requires further validation. Our findings provide insights into the unique microenvironment and clinical manifestations of MBC and generate hypotheses for future functional studies. Highlights Multi-omics profiling reveals a distinct, relatively immune-cold microenvironment in male breast cancer. PBK expression is associated with proliferation programs in MBC epithelial cells. SOX4 expression in endothelial cells is linked to an EndMT-like phenotype. KDM5D-low status is associated with reduced cGAS/STING protein levels and immune infiltration.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics for studying cell competition in the tumor microenvironment.
papers.authors: Balu P, Sureshkumar A, Sundaramurthy GD, Subramaniam G, Wong LS.
papers.abstract: Cell competition is a conserved fitness-surveillance process, first described in Drosophila epithelia, by which cells compare relative fitness with their neighbors so that less-fit "loser" cells are eliminated, extruded or forced to differentiate while fitter "winner" cells expand. In the tumor microenvironment (TME), this logic appears to be co-opted by transformed clones that eliminate normal epithelium, outcompete neighboring subclones and reshape stromal and immune compartments, making cell competition a potentially underappreciated contributor to cancer clonal evolution, immune escape and therapy resistance. Because competition is defined by a comparison between adjacent cells and by a demonstrated change in the relative representation of one population, it is difficult to resolve with bulk sequencing, which averages across precisely the heterogeneity that defines it. The convergence of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, spatial and single-cell proteomics, artificial intelligence (AI) and network-inference bioinformatics now allows competition-relevant cellular states, interfaces and signaling relationships to be measured at the resolution the problem requires. We emphasize at the outset that these technologies are, in almost all current applications, hypothesis-generating: they identify candidate competitive interfaces and putative winner and loser states from static measurements, and they do not by themselves demonstrate that competition has occurred. This review synthesizes advances across these domains; proposes an explicit three-tier evidence framework separating direct experimental evidence of cell competition from competition-relevant associations and from computational predictions; distinguishes cell competition from related processes such as clonal selection, immune editing and differential proliferation; and defines a putative cell competition network as a falsifiable construct whose edges include ligand-receptor, spatial-adjacency, metabolic and mechanical relations. We further outline a conceptual, context-dependent Cell Competition Score (CCS) as a testable specification rather than a biomarker-ready instrument, and set out the benchmarking, causal-inference and prospective-validation requirements that stand between current capability and any clinical application.

papers.title: AI-assisted single-cell transcriptomics defines immunosuppressive ecosystem states and CD274-centered communication networks in myelodysplastic syndrome.
papers.authors: Shao Y, Zhu W, Wang K, Li C, Li J, Chen H, Zhou Y.
papers.abstract: Background Defining the transcriptional ecosystem states that govern immune dysfunction in myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) is critical for identifying mechanistically grounded therapeutic targets in this heterogeneous hematopoietic malignancy. The MDS bone marrow immune ecosystem undergoes profound disease-associated remodeling that shifts from immune-mediated hematopoietic suppression in early disease to a globally immunosuppressive state that enables malignant clone expansion, yet the ecosystem-state architecture underlying this transition remains incompletely characterized. Methods We deployed an AI-assisted single-cell transcriptomic analytical pipeline-integrating unsupervised Leiden machine learning clustering, multi-modal dimensionality reduction (UMAP, t-SNE, PCA), pathway module scoring, and ligand-receptor inference-on public bone marrow mononuclear cell datasets (GSE241417 as primary MDS scRNA-seq cohort; GSE120221 as external healthy bone marrow reference) to define immune ecosystem states across 11 transcriptionally distinct cell populations. Disease-associated T/NK-cell ecosystem state remodeling, immunosuppressive cytokine and checkpoint programs, and CD274-centered intercellular communication networks were systematically characterized. Key immune regulatory genes (IL10, TGFB1, CD274, FOXP3) were validated by RT-PCR in MDS-derived cell lines, and CD274 perturbation experiments were performed to investigate its regulatory role in shaping immunosuppressive ecosystem programs. Results Eleven transcriptionally distinct immune ecosystem states were resolved within the MDS bone marrow microenvironment, with disease-associated redistribution toward cytotoxic and exhaustion-like T/NK programs. Pathway analysis revealed enrichment of T cell activation, interferon response, and cytokine signaling across ecosystem states. CD274-high cells were associated with elevated TGFB, checkpoint, and immunoregulatory module scores, while computationally inferred CD274-PDCD1 communication coexisted with TGFB1-TGFBR, LGALS9-HAVCR2, and IL10-related axes, suggesting a multi-layered immunosuppressive network. RT-PCR confirmed increased IL10, TGFB1, and CD274 expression in both MDS-derived cell lines; FOXP3 was significantly increased in SKM-1 but not significantly changed in MUTZ-1. CD274 perturbation was associated with marked IL-10 changes in SKM-1, whereas knockdown produced little apparent IL-10 reduction in MUTZ-1; FOXP3 responses were also cell-line dependent. Conclusion This study defines the MDS bone marrow immune ecosystem at single-cell resolution using AI-assisted transcriptomic analysis, identifying CD274 as a molecule associated with immunosuppressive ecosystem programs. The findings support a hypothesis-generating model in which CD274-associated signaling may coexist with cytokine and checkpoint communication networks in MDS and may inform future ecosystem-focused therapeutic studies. Further validation using primary patient-derived immune subsets and protein-level assays is required.
papers.venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology

papers.title: From metabolic reprogramming to immune homeostasis: the bidirectional regulatory network of HIF-1 α /HK2 and Th17/Treg in gout.
papers.authors: Wei L, Gan J, Cao C, Wang J, Ren Y, Wang S, Zhou M.
papers.abstract: Gout is a metabolic inflammatory disease whose pathogenesis involves the complex interaction between metabolic reprogramming and immune homeostasis imbalance. This review focuses on the bidirectional network through which the HIF-1 α /HK2 axis regulates the Th17/Treg balance via glycolytic reprogramming. Monosodium urate (MSU) crystals drive enhanced aerobic glycolysis in macrophages through the GLUT1-JNK-HIF-1 α signaling axis, where hexokinase 2 (HK2), as a metabolic checkpoint, connects glycolysis with NLRP3 inflammasome activation and neutrophil extracellular trap (NETosis)-induced M1 polarization. The glycolytic metabolic bias promotes the differentiation of T helper 17 (Th17) cells while inhibiting the generation of regulatory T (Treg) cells. In turn, cytokines derived from Th17/Treg cells reversely regulate the metabolic status of antigen-presenting cells, forming a feedback loop for inflammation amplification or resolution. Based on this network model, intervention strategies targeting the HIF-1 α /HK2/mTOR glycolytic axis and metabolic checkpoints (such as HK2, PKM2), including chaetocin, rapamycin, and various natural products, have shown therapeutic potential for restoring immune homeostasis. Current evidence mainly comes from animal models and in vitro experiments. In the future, it is necessary to use single-cell multi-omics technology to resolve the heterogeneity of the immunometabolic landscape, and to verify the dynamic regulatory mechanism of this network in the self-limiting resolution of gout inflammation.

papers.title: TMC8 is associated with a paradoxical immune landscape and promotes clear cell renal cell carcinoma progression.
papers.authors: Wang K, Zhu X, Li M, Lin L, Lin N, Zhu L, Chen J.
papers.abstract: Background Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) progression is closely linked to a complex tumor microenvironment (TME), yet key regulators remain unclear. This study aimed to systematically investigate the roles of TMC8 in ccRCC, focusing on its immunological and biological potential. Methods Multi-cohort transcriptomic data were integrated to analyze TMC8 expression and prognostic value. Functional enrichment and multiple immune deconvolution algorithms were applied to characterize TME associations. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis characterized TMC8 -associated transcriptional features across immune-cell populations. Sex-stratified analyses were performed to identify dimorphic effects. In vitro and in vivo experiments were conducted to validate the biological functions of TMC8 . Results TMC8 was significantly upregulated in ccRCC and associated with poor overall survival, particularly in males. Its expression correlated with higher estimated immune infiltration and antigen-presentation-related signatures, alongside elevated expression of exhaustion-associated markers. scRNA-seq analysis suggested the uncoupling of T-cell activation and effector competence. Notably, TMC8 exhibited marked sex-specific associations, with stronger oncogenic and immunological associations in males. Functionally, TMC8 promoted tumor progression by enhancing proliferation, migration, and invasion, which were suppressed upon TMC8 knockdown in vitro and in vivo . Conclusion TMC8 is associated with dysregulated oncogenic signaling and an immunologically active yet dysfunctional TME in ccRCC, with pronounced sex-specific associations, and may represent a putative therapeutic target warranting further validation.

papers.title: An immune-resistance dual-axis framework prioritizes MAL2 for functional investigation in lung cancer.
papers.authors: Zhang J, Luo S, Jing X, Lu X, Xiong Y.
papers.abstract: Background Immune checkpoint blockade has reshaped lung cancer treatment, yet durable benefit remains restricted to a subset of patients. Biomarkers incompletely capture interactions between immune activation and tumor-intrinsic resistance. Integrating immune and epithelial expression programs may help identify response-associated states and candidates for functional investigation. Methods Public bulk transcriptomes were analyzed with format-specific preprocessing, empirical Bayes differential expression, standardized cross-cohort evidence, and gene-set enrichment. Five discovery-informed modules formed an immune-resistance score. Conditional leave-one-out and leave-cohort-out analyses refitted normalization within training data and compared the fixed score with a nested ridge-logistic model. Survival, composition-adjustment, and prioritization sensitivity analyses were performed. Single-cell counts underwent quality control, unsupervised clustering, and patient-level pseudobulk analysis. MAL2 was investigated in A549 and H1299 cells using knockdown, growth, motility, apoptosis, HLA-ABC, cytokine, and PBMC co-culture assays. Results No individual gene met FDR Conclusion The immune-resistance framework links cohort-level response patterns to epithelial candidates for functional investigation. MAL2 depletion alters growth and immune-related phenotypes in lung cancer cells, supporting further investigation of its biological role.

papers.title: Immunological characterization of a multi-epitope vaccine against Echinococcus granulosus based on the extracellular structural domain of CTLA-4.
papers.authors: Li Y, Ma X, Jia H, Zheng J, Chen N, Zhou W, Gong Q, Zhao S, Ding J, Zhou X.
papers.abstract: Purpose The aim of this study was to provide potential for the development of an efficient multi-epitope vaccine against Echinococcus granulosus by exploring the immunological properties and immune efficacy of the recombinant antigen CTLA-4IgV-EgG1Y162-2(4) for the effective prevention of E. granulosus . Methods Target antigen sequences were retrieved from NCBI. Epitopes of CTLA-4IgV-EgG1Y162-2(4) were predicted using IEDB and SYFPEITHI, and physicochemical properties and tertiary structure were analyzed via ProtParam, ProtScale, DNASTAR, and SWISS-MODEL. The recombinant plasmid was constructed, expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3), and purified by Ni-NTA affinity chromatography, with identity confirmed by SDS-PAGE and Western blotting. Murine dendritic cells (DCs) were cultured with the recombinant protein for 24 h and analyzed by flow cytometry for maturation and antigen binding. Balb/c mice were immunized with the recombinant protein and adjuvant; DC maturation was assessed by flow cytometry, splenocyte proliferation was evaluated by CCK-8, and serum IFN-γ, IL-4, and IgG were assessed by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Immunized mice were challenged with E. granulosus ; after 120 days, the cyst wet weight inhibition rate was calculated, and spleen DC maturation, Th1/Th2 profiles, and serum cytokines were analyzed. Results The amino acid sequence of CTLA-4IgV-EgG1Y162-2(4) was obtained, and epitope analysis revealed six T-cell and B-cell co-associated epitopes, with no epitope displacement caused by the CTLA-4 extracellular region or GSGGSG linker. Bioinformatics tools successfully predicted its physicochemical properties and spatial structure. The recombinant plasmid was constructed and expressed in BL21 cells. The purified protein was confirmed by His antibody and showed specific Western blot reactivity with CE-infected sera. CTLA-4IgV-EgG1Y162-2(4) promoted DC maturation both in vitro and in vivo , enhanced splenocyte proliferation, and elevated IFN-γ, IL-4, and IgG levels. In the challenge experiment, this group showed lower infection rates and cyst wet weights, and higher Th1 and lower Th2 responses, with favorable IFN-γ/IL-4 profiles. Conclusion This study substantiates that CTLA-4IgV-EgG1Y162-2(4) stands as a multi-epitope vaccine characterized by remarkable immunogenicity and antigenicity, thus furnishing an indispensable theoretical and empirical foundation for the management and treatment of cystic echinococcosis (CE).

papers.title: CDKN3 in cancer: context-dependent cell-cycle control and implications for genome stability and therapy.
papers.authors: Li Y, Cheng L, Zhang X, Zhang Z, Du G.
papers.abstract: Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 3 (CDKN3), also known as kinase-associated phosphatase (KAP), dephosphorylates activating cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2) Thr160, yet high expression is associated with aggressive features in some cancers. This review distinguishes messenger RNA (mRNA) expression, protein abundance, phosphatase activity, functional dependency, prognostic association, and treatment-response prediction. Renal studies include selected perturbation evidence, whereas lung studies cited here primarily report prognostic or computational associations. Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) findings remain directionally discordant across analytes, etiologies, models, and endpoints. Recent triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) studies include transcriptomic and cell-perturbation evidence, as well as a separate cell and murine mammary fat-pad graft study, while an ultraviolet (UV)-induced skin-cancer study identifies a sex- and context-specific protective axis. These results do not support a universal CDKN3 role. A CDKN3-specific connection to chromosomal instability (CIN) and cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling remains unvalidated. Micronuclei and CIN do not invariably activate cGAS-STING. Bulk immune signatures and survival associations alone cannot establish direct immune regulation, functional dependency, or treatment sensitivity. This focused narrative review compares molecular measurements, genetic perturbations, clinical associations, and selected computational studies. We outline matched assays, genetic rescue, longitudinal CIN measurements, and pathway-specific tests needed to determine whether CDKN3 is a context-specific dependency, a biomarker, or a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Expression characteristics of FAM20A in stomach adenocarcinoma and its potential as a prognostic marker.
papers.authors: Ning T, Li Z, Fu Z, Li Q, Liu L, Wang J, Liu Y, Lu J.
papers.abstract: Stomach adenocarcinoma (STAD) is a prevalent malignancy that is associated with high morbidity and mortality rates globally. Current therapeutic strategies are constrained by the limitations associated with early diagnosis difficulties and personalized treatment approaches. Therefore, novel prognostic biomarkers are urgently needed to improve prognostic accuracy, facilitate risk stratification and guide personalized treatment decisions. Family with sequence similarity 20, member A ( FAM20A ) has also been implicated in lung squamous cell carcinoma and papillary thyroid carcinoma. In the present study, the expression levels and prognostic significance of FAM20A in STAD were investigated by performing bioinformatics analyses on data acquired from The Cancer Genome Atlas, Genotype-Tissue Expression project and Human Protein Atlas databases. Survival analyses revealed that elevated levels of FAM20A expression associated with worse prognosis across several cancer types, including STAD (hazard ratio=1.636; P FAM20A were enriched within immune-related pathways (such as 'immune response-regulating signaling pathway' and 'regulation of immune effector process'), suggesting its involvement in modulating the tumor immune microenvironment. Furthermore, analysis using the TIMER database identified positive correlations between FAM20A expression and infiltration by macrophages and dendritic cells (DCs). In addition, macrophage and DCs infiltration levels in gastric cancer were associated with shorter survival in patients with STAD, which could impact patient survival outcomes. Experimental analysis further demonstrated that FAM20A facilitates the proliferation, migration and invasion of stomach cancer cells. In HGC-27 gastric cancer cells transfected with a lentivirus overexpressing FAM20A or control lentivirus, a proliferation assay showed increased proliferation at 48 h, a wound-healing assay showed enhanced migration, and a Transwell assay showed increased invasion compared with controls. These results suggest that FAM20A upregulation may promote the proliferation, migration and invasion of gastric cancer cells. Collectively, these results emphasize the potential of FAM20A as a prognostic biomarker whilst elucidating its role in shaping the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Prognostic biomarker SCNM1 is associated with immune infiltration and therapeutic response, and promotes tumor migration in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.authors: Jia L, Liang Z, Wen J, Guo H, He S, Peng Y.
papers.abstract: Sodium channel modifier 1 (SCNM1) is involved in biological processes including RNA splicing and the regulation of primary cilium length; however, its role in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains largely unclear. The present study aimed to investigate the expression pattern, clinical relevance and functional significance of SCNM1 in HCC. Clinical and transcriptomic data were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas, Genotype-Tissue Expression, International Cancer Genome Consortium and Gene Expression Omnibus databases. SCNM1 expression, DNA methylation status and immune infiltration characteristics were systematically analyzed. A SCNM1-related prognostic gene signature was constructed using machine learning approaches. Cell Counting Kit-8, colony formation and Transwell migration assays were performed to evaluate the effects of SCNM1 knockdown on Huh1 cell proliferation, clonogenic capacity and migration, respectively. SCNM1 protein expression was also evaluated by immunohistochemistry in clinical tissue specimens obtained from 10 patients with HCC. SCNM1 was significantly upregulated in HCC tissues and was associated with unfavorable survival outcomes. Immunohistochemical staining further confirmed higher SCNM1 protein expression in HCC tissues than in non-tumor liver tissues. Gene set enrichment analysis indicated that SCNM1 expression was closely associated with metabolic pathways, including oxidative phosphorylation and immune-related processes. Elevated SCNM1 expression was associated with increased estimated infiltration of immune cells, including B cells and macrophages, and positively correlated with the expression of antigen processing and presentation-related genes, including human leukocyte antigen-A, transporter associated with antigen processing (TAP)1 and TAP2. Functional experiments demonstrated that SCNM1 knockdown suppressed HCC cell proliferation, clonogenic capacity and migratory ability. In addition, the SCNM1-based prognostic model effectively stratified patients with distinct survival outcomes. In conclusion, the results indicated that SCNM1 is upregulated in HCC and is associated with poor prognosis and immune-related characteristics. The SCNM1-related prognostic model may provide a useful tool for patient risk stratification and offer insights into the clinical relevance of SCNM1 in HCC.

papers.title: Clinical Risk Models, Inflammatory-Nutritional Indices and a Neural-Network Survival Model in Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
papers.authors: Sali M, Yigit E, Ardıç SD, Sali S, Coskun A, Ozcelik EE, Özmarasalı BE, Aktaş A, Sahin AB, Çubukçu E, Evrensel T, Deligönül A.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: In metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC), the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium (IMDC) and Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSKCC) risk models remain the primary tools for prognostic stratification but may not fully capture outcome heterogeneity in the contemporary treatment era. Systemic inflammatory-nutritional biomarkers such as the pan-immune-inflammation value (PIV) and the hemoglobin-albumin-lymphocyte-platelet (HALP) score have emerged as complementary, readily available prognostic indicators, yet their added value alongside established risk models, nephrectomy status, and modern predictive approaches such as machine learning remains poorly defined in real-world cohorts. This study jointly evaluated established risk models, inflammatory-nutritional biomarkers, and an exploratory neural-network survival model for prognostication in mRCC. Methods: In this retrospective, single-center cohort study, 96 patients with mRCC diagnosed and treated between January 2010 and January 2025 were evaluated, with clinical outcomes retrospectively reviewed up to a data cut-off of 17 November 2025. Clinicopathological characteristics, IMDC and MSKCC risk classification, nephrectomy status, and baseline PIV and HALP values were assessed for their association with progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) using Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression analyses. As an exploratory analysis, a dual-head neural network predicting both the risk of death and survival time was developed; feature screening and hyperparameter tuning were nested within stratified 5-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times, and the network was benchmarked on identical splits against IMDC, MSKCC, Cox, elastic-net Cox and random survival forest models. Results: At a median follow-up of 82.6 months, 77 PFS events and 57 deaths had occurred; median PFS and OS were 17.8 and 46.3 months, respectively. IMDC risk classification was significantly associated with both PFS and OS, whereas MSKCC risk classification was associated with OS but not PFS; PIV and HALP were associated with OS only. In multivariable analyses, nephrectomy status remained independently associated with both PFS and OS, whereas IMDC and MSKCC classifications remained associated with OS in separate adjusted models, although the MSKCC estimates should be interpreted cautiously because of the relatively small poor-risk subgroup. The neural network achieved a nested cross-validated C-index of 0.685 (95% CI, 0.608-0.764), comparable to a Cox model with IMDC risk group and nephrectomy status (0.692) and a random survival forest (0.695), numerically higher than the IMDC risk group alone (0.629) and higher than the MSKCC risk group alone (0.594). Its integrated Brier score was 0.189, compared with 0.164 for the IMDC-plus-nephrectomy Cox model, 0.183 for the random survival forest, and 0.221 for the Kaplan-Meier reference; its calibration slope was 0.54, indicating overly extreme predictions. Conclusions: Established risk models remained informative, particularly for OS, while nephrectomy status was the most consistent prognostic factor across conventional and neural-network analyses; PIV and HALP were associated with overall survival in unadjusted analyses but did not show independent prognostic value. An exploratory neural-network model showed discrimination comparable to conventional Cox-based models; however, its individualized survival-probability estimates had greater prediction error than those of the IMDC-plus-nephrectomy Cox model and were poorly calibrated in slope. Recalibration and external validation in larger, contemporary cohorts are required before clinical implementation.
